card.name: Arabic script inside English glosses
card.fires_on: Arabic or Persian script letters and diacritics inside English text, such as a translated word in a dictionary list or a native-script name in parentheses. Also fires on a colon introducing a quoted Quranic passage.

modes.label: Arabic letters in glosses
modes.description: Individual Arabic-script letters or vowel marks of a foreign-language equivalent placed after an English entry or name.
modes.example: a four-winged insect that makes honey. - نَحْلَـه،<< ن>>َحْـلArabic

modes.label: Native-script name after a colon
modes.description: First letter of a Persian or Arabic name given in parentheses after a language label.

modes.label: Colon before a quotation
modes.description: A colon that introduces a quoted religious statement.
modes.example: The Qur'an tells us about these people in the following words<<: >>Those are some of the Prophets

card.writes: It nudges output toward Arabic and Korean verbs and away from Arabic nouns, but the effect is weak.
card.plain: It fires on Arabic-script spellings placed inside English text, like dictionary translations or names in brackets.
